subject: Climate & Environment
title: Carbon Released by Clearing
description: A fast breakdown of Carbon Released by Clearing for builders.

hook.text: Deforestation is responsible for about 10% of all global greenhouse gas emissions.

buildup.text: When forests burn, carbon stored in wood and soil escapes into the atmosphere as CO₂.

discovery.text: Tropical deforestation alone releases about 4.8 billion tons of CO₂ every year.

twist.text: The soil beneath cleared forests keeps releasing carbon for years after the trees are gone.

climax.text: Protecting existing forests is often cheaper and faster than any carbon capture technology.

punchline.text: The cheapest carbon capture machine is the tree already standing.

quiz.question: What share of global emissions comes from deforestation?

details.summary: When forests are cleared by burning or left to decompose, stored carbon returns to the atmosphere as CO2 and methane. Tropical deforestation releases roughly 4 to 5 billion tons of CO2 per year, comparable to the entire European Union's annual emissions.
details.whyItMatters: Forest clearing converts carbon sinks into carbon sources. This double loss amplifies the climate impact of deforestation far beyond the immediate area.
takeaways: Burning releases stored carbon almost instantly as CO2 and soot
Decomposition releases carbon more slowly over years to decades
Peat forest fires can release 10 times more carbon than surface fires

faq.question: How much carbon does burning a hectare of tropical forest release?
faq.answer: A typical hectare of tropical forest stores 150 to 300 tons of carbon in biomass and soil. Burning releases most of the aboveground carbon immediately, while soil carbon continues to be released through decomposition and erosion for years.

faq.question: Why are peat forest fires especially damaging for climate?
faq.answer: Peat stores centuries of compacted organic material below the surface. When drained and ignited, peat can burn underground for months, releasing 10 times more carbon per hectare than surface forest fires and producing dense toxic haze.
